name: Hagia Sophia (Church of Holy Wisdom)
description: The architectural crown of the Byzantine Empire, featuring a revolutionary 31-meter pendentive dome that seemed to 'hang suspended from the heavens'.
history: Served as the cathedral of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople for 900 years before becoming an Ottoman imperial mosque in 1453.
construction: Constructed in just five years using brick, mortar, and precious marbles from across the empire, adorned with gold glass mosaics.
architecture: First massive square basilica covered by a circular dome on four pendentives, creating an expansive interior light space.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; defined Eastern Christian and Ottoman architecture for 1,500 years.
